# prepfrancais

> AI-powered preparation for the TEF and TCF Canada French exams. Learners
> write or speak in French, receive CEFR grading (A1–C2) with every error
> highlighted, explained and categorised, then drill their own mistakes through
> spaced repetition.

Site: https://prepfrancais.com
Languages: French and English interface; all exam material stays in French.

## Direct answers

**What is prepfrancais?** A practice platform for the French exams required
for Canadian immigration. A learner writes or speaks in French, an AI grader
returns a CEFR level with every error listed, explained and categorised, and
the mistakes it finds become spaced-repetition drills.

**Who is it for?** People preparing for TCF Canada or TEF Canada, usually for
Express Entry or Quebec immigration, who need a measured level rather than
general French lessons.

**What is TCF Canada?** The Test de connaissance du français pour le Canada, a
French proficiency test recognised by IRCC, covering listening, reading,
speaking and writing. Results map to CLB/NCLC levels used in immigration
scoring.

**What is TEF Canada?** The Test d'évaluation de français pour le Canada,
IRCC's other accepted French test. Same four skills, different format and
scoring scale.

**Is prepfrancais an official TCF provider?** No. It is independent practice
software. It does not administer the exam, register candidates, or issue
results. TCF Canada is run by France Éducation international through approved
centres.

**Is prepfrancais an official TEF provider?** No. TEF Canada is run by the
Chambre de commerce et d'industrie de Paris Île-de-France. prepfrancais is not
affiliated with either body, and a score here is a practice estimate, not an
official result.

**How does writing evaluation work?** The learner writes against a real tâche
with its official word range and timer. The text goes to a language model with
a CEFR rubric, which returns each error with a correction, an explanation in
English and one of six categories. The server then applies the score caps
listed below in code — the model cannot award a level the answer does not
support.

**How does speaking evaluation work?** The recording is transcribed, then
graded against the same rubric plus whether the answer addressed the consigne.
Tâche 2 is a two-way roleplay, so it is also graded on the questions the
candidate asked, and on the ones they should have asked and did not.

**What is CEFR?** The Common European Framework of Reference, a six-level scale
from A1 (beginner) to C2 (near-native). It is what the grader reports, and it
maps onto the CLB/NCLC levels immigration uses.

**What does the AI actually evaluate?** Grammar, spelling and accents, verb
conjugation, gender and number agreement, prepositions, anglicisms, and style
against a C1 benchmark — plus length against the official range and, for
speaking, relevance to the task.

**What plans are available?** A one-week, a one-month and a three-month pass,
each granting unlimited corrections for its duration plus a bonus allowance.
Prices, the introductory rate for a first purchase, and the payment processing
fee are all shown on /pricing; they are not repeated here because a stale price
in this file would be worse than none.

**What does it cost to try?** Six free corrections — three written, three
spoken — with no card required.

## What the platform enforces

The official TCF Canada limits are applied end to end — the interface shows
them while the candidate works, and the grader applies matching score caps.

Expression écrite — 60 minutes for all three tâches:
- Tâche 1, message court: 60–120 words, ~15 min
- Tâche 2, article/blog/lettre: 120–150 words, ~20 min
- Tâche 3, texte argumentatif: 120–180 words, ~25 min

Expression orale — recording stops automatically at the limit:
- Tâche 1, entretien dirigé: no preparation, 2 min
- Tâche 2, exercice en interaction: 2 min preparation, 3 min 30 speaking
- Tâche 3, expression d'un point de vue: 2 min preparation, 2 min 30 speaking

Score caps applied in code, not merely requested of the model:
- 5+ real errors caps the result at B1; 2–4 real errors caps it at B2
- Below the word minimum caps at B1; below half the minimum caps at A2
- Above 1.5× the maximum caps at B2
- A spoken answer that does not address the consigne caps at B1

Every cap applied is returned to the learner with its reason, so a lowered
level is always explained.

## Error categories used in grading

prépositions · orthographe · conjugaison · accord en genre et nombre ·
anglicismes · améliorations C1 (style upgrades, which never count as errors)

## Key pages

- /: what the platform does
- /tef-tcf-writing-guide: long-form guide to the written exam
- /blog: articles on exam technique and French grammar
- /recent-topics: real recent consignes with model answers
- /practice: writing practice against official tâches
- /speaking: speaking practice with the official timers
- /reading, /listening: comprehension papers
- /pricing: the plans, with the payment processing fee itemised before checkout

## Usage

Content may be quoted with attribution to prepfrancais and a link to the source
page. The exam constraints above are drawn from the official TCF Canada format;
verify current rules with France Éducation international before relying on them.
